We almost launched with the wrong label. The draft looked clean on screen, but it buried the chicory percentage on the back panel in 6-point font.

Then a retailer in Mumbai said something that stopped me: "If my mother picks this up, she won't find it. She'll just taste it and feel cheated."

We rewrote the front panel that night. Bold, Purista, Purica, and Prima now say PURE COFFEE — 0% CHICORY in bold type you can read from across the kitchen counter. Ultra Blend says 70% COFFEE, 30% CHICORY — same size, same prominence, no hiding.

That decision cost us a cheaper co-packer who refused to change the label template. We walked away.

Today, every SKU passes one test before it ships: if someone reads this jar daily for a year, will they ever feel misled?

Bold: Agglomerated pure coffee. 0% chicory.
Purista: Freeze-dried pure Robusta. 0% chicory.
Purica: Freeze-dried pure Arabica. 0% chicory.
Ultra Blend: 70% coffee, 30% chicory — stated on the front, not hidden in small print.

Revenue lost, trust kept. The label is the only contract that matters.

growth_reel_fb.title: Why Instant Coffee Disses Instantly but Premium Takes 5 Seconds
growth_reel_fb.caption:
Hey coffee lovers – have you ever poured instant coffee and watched the granules dissolve in a flash, then wondered why your favorite filter brew needs a full minute to settle? The secret lies in the particle size and the brewing method.

Instant coffee, especially the freeze‑dry version in our Purista jar, is made by removing almost all moisture, leaving tiny, airy powder that rehydrates instantly. Think of it like a fine snowflake – it spreads and dissolves in seconds.

Your regular coffee, whether brewed in a filter or French press, is a liquid extraction. The grounds sit in hot water for 3–5 minutes, allowing the oils and flavors to seep out. That extra time builds depth – a reason why a slow pour feels richer.

But here’s the kicker: if you add the instant coffee to the cup first and then pour water, the instant will stay on the bottom for a moment, just like the granules in a filter brew. Swapping the order can change the feel of your cup.

So, which method do you swear by – instant for instant gratification or brewed for depth? Let’s debate below!
